editorial:
Imagine crash-landing on a planet 65 million years before humans even existed, with nothing but a laser rifle and a scared kid to protect. That is the wild setup of 65, a sci-fi adventure that drops you straight into a survival race against time. Adam Driver plays Mills, a pilot from another world who wakes up on prehistoric Earth after a crash. The only other survivor is Koa, a young girl who does not even speak his language. Together they must cross dangerous ground filled with hungry dinosaurs to reach an escape ship before a giant asteroid slams into the planet. The whole thing feels like a tight survival story with a ticking clock that never lets up.

Driver carries the movie with a quiet, tough performance that makes you care about Mills and his lost family. The action scenes are fast and punchy, and the dinosaur designs look great on screen. The downside is the story is pretty simple and some moments feel rushed, so do not expect deep character drama. Still, if you want a quick, fun ride, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mills and Koa finally reach the escape vessel just as the massive asteroid begins its descent. They launch into space and watch from orbit as the asteroid strikes Earth, causing the extinction event that wipes out the dinosaurs. Back on their ship, Mills learns his daughter has passed away, but he finds new purpose in protecting Koa. The two head home together, surviving against all odds.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dinosaur action and quick survival thrillers.
